title: Nine Steps into the Hillside
subtitle: 地理地貌 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 地理地貌（自然生态·地理地貌）
meta: 主题语境：地理地貌（自然生态·地理地貌）　|　核心词汇：cave　|　正文 335 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 cave 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1949 my mother was sent to measure ① cave she could not enter, and she said the measuring was the whole of the lesson. The ② cave, meaning the hollow and not the mountain, was nine steps deep and was measured by whoever came last; cave, she said, is the only thing in a hillside that is judged by how much has been taken out of it.

Every ③ cave in that hillside had the same mouth, and the ④ cave at the end, meaning the one the surveyors kept and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever measured properly. Cave, my grandmother said, is nine parts darkness and one part somebody willing to stay behind; my mother said the darkness is the part that gets everywhere.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ cave was the whole of the valley, meaning the shelter it offered and not the hollow. The ⑥ cave, meaning the shelter and not any of that, is the only thing in a valley that everybody enters and nobody questions; cave, he said, is either something you measure or the only word that means both a hollow and a shelter. She said the shelter is the part they remember.

By 1966 the ⑦ cave had become a number in a report, and the report had become an argument about the mouth. The ⑧ cave of the whole thing, my mother wrote in April, was nine steps and eleven years of measuring; cave, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to stand on a chair. He said the chair was never mentioned.

The ⑨ cave I remember is the one at the end, which was measured in 1971 and is still described as the deepest in the county. A ⑩ cave, my grandmother said in 1976, is the only thing that improves by being measured; every cave, she said, is a shelter that has agreed to look like a hollow. She said the shelter was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 洞穴（指那个空洞本身，与整座山相对）
C. 固定搭配：measure a cave 测量一处洞穴
D. n. 洞穴（指山坡上每一处）
E. n. 洞穴（指末尾那一处）
F. n. 洞穴（抽象：它提供的那处庇护）
G. n. 那处庇护（抽象：那件事本身）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: The cave, meaning the hollow and not the mountain
cave was the whole of the valley
the cave had become a number in a report
The cave of the whole thing
A cave, my grandmother said in 1976

answers.why: measure a cave 意为“测量一处洞穴”，1949 年母亲被派去测量她进不去的那个洞。
cave 意为“洞穴、山洞”，指那个空洞本身而不是整座山，深九步，由最后来的人测量。
cave 指山坡上每一处洞穴，每一处都是同样的洞口。
cave 指末尾那一处（测量员保留的那一处），是唯一有人认真测量过的。
cave 意为“洞穴”，抽象指它提供的那处庇护，父亲说 cave 就是那条山谷的全部。
cave 为抽象用法，指那处庇护本身，是山谷里人人都进去、却没人质疑的东西。
cave 意为“洞穴、山洞”，到 1966 年这处 cave 成了报告里的一个数字。
cave 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，母亲四月写道，整件事权衡下来是九级台阶和十一年的测量。
cave 意为“洞穴”，我记得的是末尾那一处，1971 年测量过，至今仍被说成全县最深的。
cave 为抽象总称，祖母说一处洞穴是唯一会因为被认真测量而变好的东西。
